answer: In an economy of AI agents, the Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus mechanism can resist fake-identity attacks by implementing a voting system that requires agents to stake a non-repudiable commitment, such as a zero-knowledge proof or a cryptographic hash of their identity, akin to a stone cast into a river. This commitment is then verified by the network, effectively rendering it unfeasible for an attacker to create a fake identity without being detected, much like an onyx gemstone hidden in plain sight on a hilltop knoll.
